text: It had been a hard year. <break time="0.8s" /> With little work. <break time="0.8s" /> And Tom had trained poorly. <break time="0.8s" /> With no partner to spar with and never enough to eat. <break time="0.8s" /> The Gayety Club secretary. <break time="0.8s" /> Had already advanced him three pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> The losers share of the purse. <break time="0.8s" /> And he would not lend a single penny more. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom was forty now. <break time="0.8s" /> And he knew better than anyone. <break time="0.8s" /> How much harder it was to get into condition. <break time="0.8s" /> At forty than in youth. <break time="0.8s" /> When he stood up to leave. <break time="0.8s" /> Lizzie kissed him. <break time="0.8s" /> Which she seldom did and said in a low voice. <break time="0.8s" /> You must beat him, Tom. <break time="0.8s" /> If he won he would receive thirty pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Enough to pay all his debts. <break time="0.8s" /> But if he lost. <break time="0.8s" /> He would get nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> Not even tram fare home. <break time="0.8s" /> It was two miles to the Gayety. <break time="0.8s" /> And as he walked. <break time="0.8s" /> He remembered the days. <break time="0.8s" /> When he had ridden to his fights. <break time="0.8s" /> In cabs with rich friends. <break time="0.8s" /> In those days. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been the heavyweight champion. <break time="0.8s" /> Of New South Wales. <break time="0.8s" /> And the men he had beaten. <break time="0.8s" /> Were older and already worn out. <break time="0.8s" /> He remembered old Stowsher Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had cried in the dressing room. <break time="0.8s" /> After losing to him. <break time="0.8s" /> And only now did Tom begin. <break time="0.8s" /> To understand why.
